title: First Missing Positive
statement: A clerk numbers invoices starting from 1. Given a list `numbers` (it can contain zeros, negatives and repeats), find the **smallest positive whole number that is not in the list**.

hints.nudge: With n numbers, the answer can only be one of 1, 2, ..., n+1. Why?
hints.pattern: Use the list itself as a table: put each value v (1 <= v <= n) at index v-1.
hints.pseudocode:
for i in 0..n-1:
  while 1 <= a[i] <= n and a[a[i]-1] != a[i]: swap a[i] with a[a[i]-1]
for i in 0..n-1: if a[i] != i+1: return i+1
return n+1
hints.walkthrough: A set makes this easy in O(n) time but O(n) space. To use O(1) extra space, note the answer is at most n+1 (there are only n numbers). So only values 1..n matter. Rearrange the list so that value v sits at position v-1 by swapping (ignore values out of range and duplicates). Then scan: the first position i where a[i] != i+1 means i+1 is missing. If every position is right, the answer is n+1.
